action: Cole knelt at the spring, running cold water over his hands, already planning the tank and filter lines.
thought: Water changes everything. Now we build.

action: Maggie came down from the cabin with empty buckets, watching her family muddy and grinning at the spring.
thought: One good thing on day one—really good.

action: Sawyer crouched beside Cole, running the logistics through his head: filter, tank, gravity feed.
thought: This means no more haul days for water.

action: Finn stood grinning over the trickle of water, vindicated and buzzing with plans.
thought: I knew it! I actually knew it!

action: Bear splashed his hands in the icy water, laughing at how cold it was, soaking his sleeves.
thought: This is the best cold water ever!

description: The spring breaks through on the ridge where Finn urged them to dig, and the family gathers muddy and grinning—Cole assessing the flow, Sawyer thinking logistics, Finn vindicated, Bear splashing, Maggie arriving from the cabin with buckets.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Finn, you absolute legend. You called this.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: I told you! I TOLD you it'd be here!

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: It's so cold! Put your hand here, put your hand here!

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: This changes everything. We won't have to haul water.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: How far's the cabin from here?

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Fifty, sixty yards uphill. We can gravity-feed to a tank.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: You'd need PVC and a pump, yeah?

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Maybe just gravity and a simple filter first. We'll rig it.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: Can we dig deeper? Make it bigger?

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: We could, but let's not mess with nature here. This is good.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: Is it safe to drink?

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: We should boil it first, test it. But yes, this is real.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: For now we collect and boil. Come fall, we'll build proper.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: How much can we use a day?

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: As much as comes. Seems pretty steady. Good find, Finn.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: We should make it a place. Like, a water spot.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: With a bucket!

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: We'll need containers, anyway. This is good work today.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Everyone helped dig. This was a team thing.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: We should mark the path, keep it clear.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: And protect it from animals.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: Can bears drink from it?

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: They do. That's fine. It's their land too.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Alright. Bring some buckets up here before dinner. Let's fill them.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: On it.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: I'll help carry!

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Good. Water for tonight, and we'll keep containers full.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: First win of the season. Not bad for day one.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: Told you so.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Yes, you did. Come on, everyone—let's get water before lunch.

action: Settles at the table with a warm cup, watching his family gather as the long light fades golden outside.
thought: The land gave us what we came for.

action: Brings the pot from the stove and starts serving bowls of soup, calling everyone in from the evening.
thought: This is how we build a home here.

action: Washes his hands at the basin and pulls up a seat at the table, still thinking about the day's work.
thought: A good day. We're actually doing this.

action: Sits down with barely-contained energy, already talking about tomorrow's plans for the water collection system.
thought: I knew it. The spot was perfect.

action: Climbs into a chair next to Maggie, rubbing his eyes tiredly but grinning, muddy from head to toe.
thought: Warm cabin, full belly, family here.

description: The spring flows cold and clear on the ridge where Finn found it; now evening settles, and all five gather warm in the cabin over steaming soup, muddy and grinning, all together.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Hands washed, everyone? You're all still covered in mud.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: Do I have to? I want to eat NOW!

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: Hands, dude. Then we talk about the spring.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: Finn was right about where to dig. Good call.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Better than good. He nailed it.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: I KNEW it. The land wanted us to find it.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: The land and your instinct. Come on, everyone.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: What's for dinner? I'm starving!

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Soup and fresh bread. Nothing fancy but warm.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Fancy enough after today.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: We did good work, all of us.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: You did. And you'll do more tomorrow.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: Tomorrow we build the collection box, right?

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: We start on it. Needs to hold water all winter.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: All winter? The spring freezes?

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: We'll figure that out when it gets close.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: How much time do we have?

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Nine weeks, give or take. Plenty to work with.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: We can patch the whole cabin in nine weeks!

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: Maybe. If we focus and don't get stuck.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: One step at a time. Eat now. Plan later.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Smart woman. Come on, boys, dig in.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: Is it hot?

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Straight from the stove. Be careful.

action: He settles at the table with his rough sketch of tomorrow's water-system layout, pencil in hand.
thought: Water on day one. The land gives back.

action: She clears soup bowls from the table, listening to Cole's sketches and the boys' chatter, settling in alongside Bear who leans against her.
thought: Finn found the spring. We're actually doing this.

action: He listens to Cole's plan from near the stove, turning the logistics in his mind—less water haul means more hours for building.
thought: Less water work. More time for building.

action: He paces the small cabin, buzzing with the spring's discovery still fresh, asking Cole questions about pipe routing and when they start laying it.
thought: I knew that spot was right all along.

action: He nestles against his mother's side, eyes heavy with the day's excitement and exhaustion, listening to talk of springs and systems and tomorrow's early light.
thought: Best day ever. Best first day.

description: Evening gathers the family in the warm cabin, the water find bright in their minds—Finn buzzing, Cole planning, Maggie tending the quiet joy, Sawyer thinking logistics, Bear going sleepy.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: Did you see how clear it was?

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Finn had the eye for it.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: So we don't haul from the creek?

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Not for drinking and cooking, no.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Cuts our daily work in half easily.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: That spot felt right from the start.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: It was so cold.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Cold and clean. That's what we need.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: When do we build the system?

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Tank tomorrow, pipes the day after.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: Can we check it at first light?

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: You and me both. Need the flow.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Not in darkness.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: First light. I'm thinking around five.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: Bears come out at first light.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: So do we.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: Smart, not fearless.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Eat more before anyone goes anywhere.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: She's right about everything.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: I want to see the spring tomorrow night.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: Can we all go together?

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: If the work allows, we will.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: We'll make it happen. Days like this—you remember them.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: Water on day one. That's not luck.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: I knew where to look.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: And we trusted you. That matters.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: Best day.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Best first day ever.

action: Checks the wood stove's coals and kindles a fresh flame for the morning, then sets water to heat for coffee.
thought: Water system today. Need to move fast.

action: Gathers flour, eggs, and what butter is left in the cold box to start pancakes on the range.
thought: Food's low. Need a plan for the garden.

action: Steps outside briefly to check the morning weather, then settles in to listen to Dad's plans for the day.
thought: Clear day. Good for heavy work ahead.

action: Bounces out of bed and rushes to the main room, already asking what needs doing.
thought: Today's gonna be awesome. I can feel it.

action: Wakes more slowly, rubs his eyes, and wanders out to find his place at the table.
thought: Warm cabin, breakfast smell, everything's perfect.

description: The wood stove ticks gently, still warm from the night; Cole sets water to boil while Maggie starts pancakes, and the boys emerge one by one into the golden morning light and the smell of coffee and flour.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Stove's still got a good bed of coals this morning.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Coffee's on the way.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: Is it breakfast time? I'm so hungry!

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: Me too, me too!

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: Clear day. You can see forever out there.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Pancakes today. Bear, can you set the table?

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: On it!

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: Can I help crack the eggs?

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Right over the bowl this time. Mind the shells.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: I won't get any in. Promise.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: We'll see.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: School starts after breakfast—math and reading.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: Already? We just woke up!

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: That's how it works. We've got daylight.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: After lessons, though, we map out the water line.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: The system from the spring to the cabin?

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Right. Run it down from the ridge into a cistern nearby.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: That's a long day of digging and pipe work.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: But it saves carrying water every single day.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: Can I help dig? Please?

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: I want to help too!

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: After school, both of you. Sawyer, I'll need you steady.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: On the foundation work?

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Water today. Foundation later. Building as we go.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: This is the season. Every hour counts before winter.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: How long until winter?

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Months yet. But we work like it's coming tomorrow.

action: Cole marks the water line from the spring toward the cabin, checking elevation and distance, moving steadily with Sawyer at his side.
thought: One day for the lines, two for the catch.

action: Maggie clears the school books from the table and sets out bread, cheese, and fish for the midday meal.
thought: Finish lessons, feed them, send them back out.

action: Sawyer follows Cole's instructions carefully, learning the water line slope and marking distances with attention and thoughtful small questions.
thought: I'm actually building this with Dad.

action: Finn finishes his last math problem and darts outside toward the water work, eager to help and already thinking of ways to speed things up.
thought: This is way cooler than math.

action: Bear helps Maggie set the table, carrying the bread and asking what's for lunch, eager to eat and get back outside.
thought: Help Mom, eat fast, go outside.

description: At midday, Cole and Sawyer mark the water line from the spring toward the cabin while Finn joins them from lessons; back at the cabin porch, Maggie and Bear set the table with lunch, the endless summer light warming the whole homestead.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Water won't wait. The run is steeper than I thought.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Lunch first, water later?

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Smart. Sawyer, you getting the lay of it?

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: Yeah. The drop from the spring to the cabin is about forty feet?

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Close enough. That's good gravity.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Finn, you figure we can have the lines run by tomorrow?

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: Like, actual water flowing to the cabin?

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: That's the idea. Gravity and wood for now, beats hauling buckets.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: Can I help dig?

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: After your letters are done, you can.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: What about the cabin patching though?

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Two things at once. Water's the urgent one.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: Can we use the pipes from the truck bed?

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: No. I want those for later. Using what's on site.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: What about the weather holding?

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Clear for four days at least. We've got time.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: Can moose drink from our water system?

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: That's... actually a good question.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: It'll run downhill away from the cabin. We'll be fine.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: So tomorrow we test it all?

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Get the lines done today, test it, seal the leaks, build a catch tank.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Eat now, work steady, dinner's ready by sundown.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: Can I work the water with you the whole time?

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Absolutely. You're my lead on this.

thought: Water first, then food catches up.

action: Maggie spreads the remaining stores on the porch table, counting rations and planning how to stretch them through tomorrow.
thought: Three days left. Then Finn fishes.

action: Sawyer follows Cole's lead, learning where the water flows fastest and how to position the intake for clean, cold supply.
thought: Dad trusts me. I can do this work.

action: Finn splashes downstream from the intake, calling back findings and pulling back willows that block the line's path.
thought: Fish are here. I know they are.

action: Bear sorts through the supply box for cordage and helps Maggie check the dry goods and cans, asking when dinner is.

dialogue.line: Water flows good here. We can dig down.

dialogue.line: How deep do we need to go?

dialogue.line: Just below the surface. Keep it clean, let gravity do the work.

dialogue.line: That's your dinner, friend. Be patient.

dialogue.line: We're good. Just need to be efficient now.

dialogue.line: Similar idea. Slow, patient, let the creek provide.

dialogue.line: Can I fish too?

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: You fall in every time.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: So?

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: After we eat, buddy. Before dark.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: All of you are learning where home feeds itself.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: That's weird and cool at the same time.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: It's just cool.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Give it time, Saw. Weird becomes normal fast.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: The cans we brought will help us through next week.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: By then the garden's up. Finn catches fish.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: What about before the garden's big?

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: The land around here is generous. We just have to be smart.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: Is it dark yet?

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Still hours of light, buddy. Help me with the water barrel.

action: Maggie sets out a warm dinner on the porch—sparse portions but filling—stretching what's left to feed five.

action: Sawyer sits at the porch table, tired and proud after a full day of water-line work, listening to Dad's plans for tomorrow.

action: Finn perches at the table, animated and hungry, recounting the willows and the creek water and spinning plans for fishing tomorrow.
thought: Tomorrow we fish for real.

action: Bear sits next to Finn, tired and curious, eating quickly while asking questions about water and foundation and when they fish.

dialogue.line: Spring's running clear. Good intake.

dialogue.line: You two built something today. Come eat.

dialogue.line: We cleared so many willows!

dialogue.line: Can I have more? I'm starving.

dialogue.line: You've got plenty. Make it last.

dialogue.line: Finn, eat your vegetables.

dialogue.line: Priorities. And we've got to think about supplies soon.

dialogue.line: Town run is due. Maybe this weekend.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: Can I come?

dialogue.line: Me too! Please!

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: We'll see. But somebody has to fish.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: I could stay and work the cabin.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: That'd be good. Foundation posts tomorrow.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: Foundation? Like, digging?

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Deep holes. The real work.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Eat first. Build after.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: This food's not much.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: It's what we've got. And it's good.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: Tomorrow's going to be long.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Good long. The kind we came for.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: When does it get dark?

dialogue.line: Barely does. That's why we work.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: And eat.

dialogue.line: And eat.

action: Stands by the warm wood stove, reviewing the day's water work and thinking ahead to the foundation push.
thought: Six weeks light, so much to build.

action: Tends the fire and settles the cabin for the night, watching her tired but satisfied boys.
thought: Tired and hungry but together—that's the win.

action: Rests by the stove with legs stretched out, absorbing the deep satisfaction of a day's honest work.
thought: We built something solid. More waits.

action: Paces near the cabin door, restless and eager, already imagining tomorrow's creek and the salmon waiting.
thought: Tomorrow I fish. There are salmon there.

action: Sits close to the warmth, fighting sleep but losing, eyes heavy and content.
thought: This cabin's so warm. This feels like home.

dialogue.line: Well, that's the last of the flour used up tonight.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: We're out of food? Like, completely?

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Tomorrow morning, Finn's the hunter. Tonight we rest easy.

dialogue.line: You and me built something solid today, son.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: The intake's going to hold, isn't it?

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Through the worst of it. That's the work right there.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: Can we fish early tomorrow? Like, right when it's light?

dialogue.line: I'm coming fishing too, right?

dialogue.line: You can come, but you have to be quiet.

dialogue.line: I can be quiet.

dialogue.line: No, you can't.

dialogue.line: I CAN be quiet when it matters!

dialogue.line: Quiet is overrated. The real question is whether we'll catch anything.

dialogue.line: There's salmon in that creek. I know it.

dialogue.line: Kid, you've known a lot of things that turned out to be true.

dialogue.line: That means the water system has to stay solid.

dialogue.line: Everything's connected. Water, food, shelter. Do one well, the others follow.

dialogue.line: Dad, is that why you said foundation's next?

dialogue.line: Smart kid. We can't winterize what's not standing straight.

dialogue.line: So tomorrow we fish, but soon we're working the footings?

dialogue.line: Soon as Finn brings home dinner, yeah.

dialogue.line: This cabin is warm though. Like, really warm.

dialogue.line: The stove's doing its job. And you're all here, so it's home.

dialogue.line: Two days and I already can't imagine leaving.

dialogue.line: Yeah.

dialogue.line: That's the only thing that matters, honestly.

dialogue.line: Can we stay forever?

action: Finn hears the day's plan and bounces with barely-contained energy, afternoon fishing already filling his mind.
thought: I'm fishing salmon this afternoon.

dialogue.line: Long enough to see us through winter if we're smart. That's all we need.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Garden's coming in soon. The creek's full of fish. We'll make it.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Sawyer, grab the supplies—tarps, rope, anything we've got left. We eat quick and climb.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: On it, Dad.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: Be careful up there, you two.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Always. We're not taking chances.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: And we'll make something cool while you work!

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: You sure will, buddy.

action: Cole directs Sawyer on the roof while teaching proper technique for removing soft wood and securing new framing.
thought: Sawyer's got the knack for this. Trust him.

action: Maggie sits on the porch with water bottles and a pencil, calculating supplies for the town run she knows can't wait past tomorrow.
thought: Food won't wait. We leave at first light.

action: Sawyer climbs the makeshift frame with Cole, watching where rot has weakened the beam and learning to feel his way through the repair.
thought: Dad trusts me. I can feel the difference.

action: Finn races back and forth between the cabin's side and the supplies, hauling boards, asking questions, burning off months of restlessness in real work.
thought: Real work, finally. This is what I needed.

action: Bear hangs close, keeping the nail count steady, fetching water, and calling up jokes to keep the mood buoyant despite the afternoon's heat and hunger.
thought: Big kids work is amazing. I'm helping real.

description: Cole and Sawyer patch the cabin's south side while Finn brings boards and Bear shouts from below; Maggie tends water on the porch, her town-run list at hand—the family spread but unified, the afternoon bent toward one urgent job.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Hold it steady. You've got the angle right.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: This whole section's soft. What do we do?

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: We remove the bad and shore it underneath. You're watching right.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: How many more boards? I'll grab them!

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Water break in five, boys.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: I'm the official keeper of nails up here.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: You've been holding the same handful the whole time.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: Best handful in the whole territory.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: Cole, should the frame sit a little higher?

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Good question. Actually lower—better support underneath.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Come drink. All of you. Now.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: I like being told what to do when water's involved.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: Can't we keep going? We're on such a roll!

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: You burn out, you're no good to me. Drink.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: Will we finish the whole section today?

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Part of it is progress. Tomorrow we make town for more.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: The roof's the priority. Everything else waits.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: How much longer until it's solid?

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Few more hours of good light. We'll be solid past halfway.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: My arms are tired and I like the feeling.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: That's how you know you did something real.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: That's exactly right. Come on, eat something small.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: I can feel where the work needs to happen now.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: That's the real skill. Let's get back to it.

action: Cole sits on the cabin porch with Maggie, watching the family gather as evening light fades, quietly proud of the day's work and Sawyer's growing capability.
thought: Sawyer's got the knack for this.

action: Maggie sits beside Cole, her town-run list in hand, calmly talking through supplies and priorities with the boys settling around the porch.
thought: Sixty dollars, and we make it stretch.

action: Sawyer sits nearby listening to the evening talk, feeling the quiet pride of a full day's work on the roof patch alongside Cole.
thought: Dad trusts me with real work now.

action: Finn sits on the front steps with Bear, restless with wanting to do more despite his healing ribs, eager for the evening's talk.
thought: I could do real work if I wasn't healing.

action: Bear sits on the steps with Finn, cracking jokes to keep the mood light and listening to the plans for tomorrow's town run.
thought: Mom's coming back with food tomorrow.

description: As evening light fades to long twilight, the family gathers around the cabin porch after a day of solid patching work; Maggie plans tomorrow's crucial town run, Cole reviews the roof progress with Sawyer, all hungry, all hopeful.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: First light tomorrow. Fuel first, then food.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: We'll have you moving by five.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: The south side of the roof—is it waterproof now?

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Solid enough. We've got sixty percent of the whole patch done.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: I want to help more when you get back.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Your ribs are still healing. You're doing plenty.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: He brought every board up today. That's real work.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: It doesn't feel like real work.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: Real work is anything that matters. I'm helping too!

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: You're keeping us laughing. Don't discount that.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: How much money do we have?

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Sixty. Stretching it as far as it goes.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: We've done more with less.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: True. But I won't risk a breakdown out there.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: How long will you be gone?

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: There and back in one cycle, if the road's clear.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: What if it's not?

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Then I call the house phone and we figure it out.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: She'll be back. She's done this before.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: And she's coming back with FOOD.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Assuming the store isn't picked over.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: What are you hoping for?

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Flour, salt, sugar, eggs if they have fresh ones.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: And something green?

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: If the garden isn't producing yet, yes.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: The lettuce is close.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Another week and we'll have fresh salad.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: Salad is how you know spring won.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Summer, actually. But I see your point.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: All right, boys. Kitchen in the morning before I leave.

action: Reviews the afternoon's roof progress with Maggie at the porch table while the family gathers near the warm cabin.
thought: Building something real. One day at a time.

action: Checks her supply list one final time as Bear rests against her, fevered and slow from his sickness.
thought: Sixty dollars. Make it stretch like always.

action: Returns from the work site with scattered tools, ready to rest after a day of real work alongside his father.
thought: Dad trusts me. That changes everything.

action: Stretches carefully on the porch steps, watching the patched roof in the lengthening twilight, proud despite his healing soreness.
thought: I helped today. My body will catch up.

action: Dozes against his mother, warm and feverish, listening to the adults plan and the older boys settle in for the night.
thought: Mom always makes it better somehow.

description: The family clusters around the porch as twilight fades: Cole and Maggie plan tomorrow's run, Sawyer finishes the day's tools, Finn rests watching their work, and Bear dozes fever-warm against his mother.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: The roof's looking good. You felt the difference today, Sawyer.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: I felt a lot of things. Tired mostly.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: That's the good kind of tired. You earned it.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: I helped too, even just holding boards.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: You both did. Everyone did what they could.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: We're a real team now.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: Seventy-one percent, right?

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Seventy-one. Another day like today, and we hit eighty.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: I'll be back before dark with supplies. The roof will keep.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: The truck ready?

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Tank's clean, route's mapped. We'll be fine.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: Don't forget salt. And honey.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: Honey's important.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Never forget the honey.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: Sixty dollars is tight.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Sixty dollars and five hungry people. It works.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: It always works.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: Because we make it work.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: Mom's magic.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Mom's not magic. She's just relentless.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Same thing up here.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: Come on, Bear. Let's get you inside by the stove.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: With Mom?

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Come on, buddy. Inside where it's warm.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: I'll bring in more wood before bed.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: I can help with that.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Your foot needs rest. Let me and Sawyer handle it.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: I've got it, Dad.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Good night, all of you. Tomorrow's early.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Sleep well. We've earned it.

action: Cole fills water bottles and checks the fishing lines, practical and calm.
thought: Fish are the answer. We can do this.

action: Maggie tends Bear's fever, speaking quietly with Cole, then pulls on her boots to head down to the creek.
thought: Bear's hot. But the water will help us.

action: Sawyer lays out three fishing lines on the porch rail, checking each while watching Finn, ready to teach.
thought: They're counting on me to teach them right.

action: Finn bounces nearby help-eager, healing rib tender as he watches Sawyer work the lines.
thought: My body's slow but I can catch fish.

action: Bear sits on the porch step wrapped in his blanket, feverish but watching, determined to come along.
thought: I'm so hungry. But I want to try.

description: The cupboard bare and Bear feverish, the family gathers on the cabin porch for a quick counsel—no food left, but a clear plan: fish before noon, eat supper.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: The stores are gone, folks. Breakfast is river water and hope.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: We've caught twenty before in a morning. We can do it.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: I can show Finn and Bear how to hold the line right.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: I've watched you a hundred times, Saw. I can do this.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: Can I come even though I feel kind of terrible?

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: You stay close to me, bud. Watch from the bank.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Everyone drinks water first. Thirst makes you make mistakes.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: The run should be good this time of year.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: I can feel the fish out there already, I know it.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: We get them in by noon, I can make a proper supper.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: A supper? Like really supper?

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Fresh fish, clear water, full bellies. That's the goal today.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: I'll teach you both careful. No fancy stuff, just steady.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Sawyer, you're a good son. Thank you for this.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: It's what we do. We look out for each other.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: Let's go get them. Let's go right now.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Gear first, enthusiasm second—you know the way.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: Finn's so excited he might scare the fish.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Okay, boots on. Let's get to the creek.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Stay together. Water's cold but the light is long.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: Come on, brothers. We've got fish to catch today.

action: Cole wades into the creek shallows, showing Sawyer and Finn where the salmon pools gather in the current.
thought: Fish are the answer. We can do this.

action: Maggie keeps Bear close at the creek's edge, her hand steady on his shoulder, watching the water and his fever alike.
thought: Bear's hot. But the water will help us.

action: Sawyer stands hip-deep in the creek, coaching Finn on casting angle and line tension while keeping an eye on Bear.
thought: They're counting on me to teach them right.

action: Finn stands in the shallows, rod ready, body aching but focus sharp on the water where the salmon move.
thought: My body's slow but I can catch fish.

action: Bear wades carefully into the creek with Cole's steadying hand, determined to help fish despite the fever heat in his chest.
thought: I'm so hungry. But I want to try.

description: At the creek in bright afternoon sun, the Wilders fish for supper—Cole steady in the shallows, Sawyer coaching Finn, Maggie keeping watch over feverish Bear, all focused and hungry and hopeful.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Easy on the cast—let the water do the work.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: Finn, see how Dad keeps the line loose?

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: I got it—there's one! Wait, no—

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: Did you see it? Did you see it?

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: You're getting close, buddy.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: That's the idea. This part takes patience.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: Watch the current—they rest there.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: My arms are tired already.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: That's alright. We have time.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: I can feel one, I think?

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: You're doing great, Bear. Rest a moment if you need.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: No, I want to catch one too.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: Then you will. Like this—see?

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: How's the water feel, Finn?

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: Cold. Really cold. It's good though.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: Watch Dad's feet—he knows the bottom.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: This spot here's good. Right where the current breaks.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: There! There's a big one!

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: Where? Where?

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Easy, we've got all afternoon.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Slow and steady wins the day, boys.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: You feeling it, Finn?

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: I think—maybe—yes! I caught one!

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: You did! You did!

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: That's supper right there.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: One down. Let's get another.

action: Works steady in the shallows, calling quiet tips to Sawyer and watching the boys learn, one eye always on Bear.
thought: The boys are learning. That's what matters now.

action: Sits on the bank beside Bear, offering cool creek water and watching his fever, steady and close.
thought: We're feeding our family. Even like this.

action: Stands chest-deep, steady hand on Finn's shoulder, coaching Bear into the water, his voice patient and clear.
thought: They're listening. I can teach them.

action: Follows Sawyer's every word, feels his line tug, and whoops as his first fish breaks the surface.
thought: I caught one! I actually caught one!

action: Wades in shallow water near Maggie, tired and fever-light but smiling, trying his line again and again.
thought: I cast it myself. I'm doing this.

description: At the sun-bright creek, Sawyer guides Finn's rod taut; the fish breaks the surface and Finn whoops—Bear cheers from the shallows, Cole nods slow, and Maggie steadies Bear's shoulder.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: Keep your tip up—there, feel that tug? You got one.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: I got one! It's so strong!

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Hold steady. Let him run if he needs to.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: It's bending so far!

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: You're doing it. Just keep the line tight.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: That's beautiful, Finn. You did it.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: Is this what you feel every time, Sawyer?

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: Every time. And it never gets old. Reel him in.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: Can I try the big rod?

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: When you're stronger. Sawyer's rod fits you better.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: Come here, Bear. I'll show you the cast.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: Is the water gonna help me feel better?

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: That's exactly what it's doing. Here, drink some.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: It's so cold and good.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Sawyer, teach him the stance like you showed Finn.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: Okay, Bear—feet apart, rod back, then smooth and easy.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: Like this?

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: Perfect. Now cast.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: I did it! Did I do it right?

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: You cast it way farther than I did the first time.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Eyes on your line. Something might be already there.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: I feel something! It's moving!

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: That's it—reel slow, keep the tip up.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: You're doing this, baby. You're doing so good.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Six fish by supper, and we eat like kings.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: We're gonna make it, aren't we? We really are.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: We're already doing it.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: One day at a time, and today we're winning.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: Can we come back tomorrow?

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Every day until the run slows, bud. Every day.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: Let's get four more before the light changes.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: I'm going back in. Come on, Bear!

action: Cole rested on the cabin porch after processing the day's catch, watching the boys recover from hard work.
thought: Three days' eating, maybe even four.

action: Maggie tended the broth and stew inside the cabin, her hands warm by the stove as she settled feverish Bear nearby.
thought: Real food tonight. We're going to be OK.

action: Sawyer rested on the porch beside Finn, both boys bone-tired but proud, knowing they'd done something important today.
thought: They listened. I taught them real.

action: Finn sat beside Sawyer on the porch, his arms aching but his chest full, unable to stop thinking about that first catch.
thought: I caught one myself. Sawyer taught me good.

action: Bear rested by the warm stove inside the cabin, wrapped up and feverish but smiling at the smell of dinner.
thought: I cast it myself. I'm doing this.

description: Evening gathers the Wilders around warmth: the day's catch is simmering inside as Maggie tends both the broth and Bear, while Sawyer and Finn rest on the porch, all tired and finally full after a hard, hopeful day.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: That's three solid fish—we can eat tonight and dry some for tomorrow.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Water's hot. I'll get the broth going.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: Finn's hook didn't tangle once today. He's getting it.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: My arms are dead, but—yeah, I'm getting it.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: Sawyer said I cast it perfect.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: You all did perfect.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Cole, bring those inside? Oven's ready.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Coming.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: Bear, you want to sit by the stove?

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: Yeah. I'm cold.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Here, let's get you warm.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: Tomorrow we fish again?

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: If the light holds and Bear's better.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: I'll be better by tomorrow.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Rest does that.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: Finn, there's a deep spot on the far bank.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: Yeah? We should try it.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: If Cole says it's safe, we could.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: The broth smells like home.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: It really does. First time in weeks.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: How long until dinner?

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Twenty minutes. Wash up, you're all scales.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: I can smell it from here.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Tonight, we eat together. That matters most.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Come on. Dinner's nearly ready.

action: Cole settles on the porch with tea, watching the night and thinking about the day's small victories.
thought: The boys are learning. That's what matters.

action: Maggie sits by the warm stove, checking Bear's forehead and keeping him close as he fights sleep.
thought: He's warm. We're going to be okay.

action: Sawyer rests on the porch beside Cole, quietly proud of how his brothers listened and learned today.
thought: I taught them something real. They listened.

action: Finn sprawls beside Sawyer and Cole on the porch, exhausted but grinning about his own catch.
thought: I caught one myself. I can do this.

action: Bear leans against Maggie by the warm stove, eyes heavy but a small smile on his face.
thought: I caught one. I'm really doing this.

description: After a day of teaching and learning, the Wilders settle warm and full around the glowing stove, tired but hopeful, Maggie tending sick Bear while Cole and the boys rest nearby.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: How's your shoulder, bud? Any better?

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: Yeah. Warm now.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: You did good out there, Sawyer. Real good.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: They listened. That's the thing.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: I caught one! All myself!

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: You both did. Eat slow though—we'll make it last.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: This'll get us through a few more days.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: Maybe a week if we're careful.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: Can we go again tomorrow?

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: One day at a time, bud.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: I cast it myself, did you see?

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: I saw. You're a natural.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: The boy's got talent.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: Just needed to learn the motion.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: Can you teach me more tomorrow, Sawyer?

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: If the fish are still biting.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: For now, sleep. It's been a long day.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Best kind of long day.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: Yeah...

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: My arms feel like jelly.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: Good jelly.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: That's exhaustion, son. And it's earned.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: All of you, rest. Tomorrow will come soon enough.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: She's right. We did good. Real good.

action: Up before full light, checks the roof patching and plans the day's work with a steady eye toward winter.
thought: This roof won't last another winter.

action: Nurses her shoulder while rationing the last of yesterday's catch into a thin breakfast for five hungry people.
thought: Make it stretch. Keep them moving.

action: Wakes ready to work, joins Cole at the roof to assess the north section before eating breakfast.
thought: I can help finish this. I'm ready.

action: Bounces out of bed and fills the water bucket from the creek, then circles the porch looking for something to help with.
thought: Keep moving, keep going, that's the way.

action: Slow morning waking, gravitates to the warm stove and settles against Maggie while eating the thin breakfast she's made.
thought: Warm and food. That's enough right now.

description: Summer Day 8 breaks clear and endless; Maggie rations the last of yesterday's catch while Cole and Sawyer eye the roof, Finn fills the water bucket, and Bear leans into the stove's warmth.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Come eat while it's warm.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Sawyer, let's see that north corner before we move anything.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: It's still solid wood underneath—should hold another patch.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: Dad, I filled the bucket from the creek!

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Good man. Set it by the stove.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: I'm cold again.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Come here, then.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: How long will this section take us?

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: A day, maybe two if we do it right. No rushing.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: Can I help? Can I hammer?

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Everyone eats first. You're all fading.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: She's right. We work better on a full belly.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: Is there enough?

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: It's enough. It has to be.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: Mom, this is the same as yesterday.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Same fish, different day. Still good.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: I like it anyway!

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: You sitting down?

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: After I see they're fed.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Sit now. I can watch them.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Just for a minute.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: Your shoulder hurting?

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Old news. We've got work to do.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: The roof first. Water and wood after.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: And fishing? Can we fish?

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: After the roof. Let's not build two projects at once.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: The roof's more important anyway, right?

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: Winter doesn't wait.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Neither does hunger, so eat.

action: Working on the cabin roof with Sawyer, framing the peak and teaching the knack with patient corrections.
thought: Roof's the thing. Sawyer's got it.

action: Conducting a midday math lesson at the cabin porch, working with Finn and Bear on counting and food rationing.
thought: Stretch what we have. Keep them strong.

action: Learning the roof framing from Cole, focused and steady, checking measurements and calling his cuts right.
thought: I'm getting this. Really getting this.

action: At the porch with Maggie, trying to focus on the lesson while watching the roof work in the distance.
thought: I could help with that roof.

action: Sitting at the porch with Maggie, listening to the lesson and leaning into the warmth of her steady presence.
thought: When's lunch? I'm so hungry.

description: Maggie teaches Finn and Bear at the porch while the roof work accelerates nearby—the day balanced between the pressing build and the family's gnawing hunger.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: All right, Finn. If we have six caught fish and four go to tomorrow—

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: We'd have two today. So we eat two?

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: And I'm adding one more from yesterday's cache. Three meals, three of us on lessons.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: I want more than one fish, though.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: I know, bud. We'll make it stretch with what we have.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Sawyer, hand me that board—

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: Got it, Dad. This one?

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: That's the one. Fit's good.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: Look how fast they're going.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Eyes here, Spark. Two families of fish. How much do we have per family?

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: Um... one and a half each?

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Close enough. You're getting it.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: I'm so tired and so hungry.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Your body's healing and wants fuel. That's honest hunger.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Roof's coming together! Sawyer's a natural!

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: Thanks, Dad. Next board?

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: That's your father being proud. It's a good thing.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: Can I help with the roof after lessons?

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Your brothers might teach you when the light's still good.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: I could help too when I'm less tired.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: You'll get there, Bear. Right now you rest.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: This math is solid, Finn. You're sharper than you think.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: I want to be as sharp as Sawyer with real work.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: You will be. But read first, build second. That's the deal.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: Story after eating?

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: After you eat and rest, I'll read while your brothers build.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: Dad, should I cut this board or leave it long?

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: What do you think?

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: It's a foot too long if we're keeping the slope even.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: There you go. Trust that eye.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: And that's your lesson, boys. Work teaches you what books can't.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: But we still do the books, right?

action: Cole works the roofline with Sawyer, measuring and fitting the final beams while the afternoon light holds steady and endless.
thought: This beam's the right one. We're almost there.

action: Maggie readies a meager dinner at the cabin porch, stretching fresh fish with garden greens while keeping one eye on the work.
thought: Make it fill them. Make it count.

action: Sawyer steadies each new beam while Cole guides him, learning to feel how the frame sits and holds true.
thought: I'm getting this. I really am.

action: Finn hauls material bundles up to the roofline, eager and bouncing with energy despite the afternoon heat and hunger.
thought: We're building something real. Right now.

action: Bear trails Maggie at the porch, watching dinner prep and bouncing with restless hunger, too wound up to sit still.
thought: When can we eat? I'm so hungry.

description: The roof work locks in; Cole and Sawyer measuring beams while Finn hauls below bouncing with effort, and Maggie preps thin dinner at the porch with Bear close beside her, hungry and hopeful.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: This beam's solid. Nice work, Saw.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: It's starting to feel right, Dad.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: That's the feeling you keep chasing.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: Can I nail that one?

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Already set, bud. Grab that bundle for me?

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Folks, dinner's coming up soon.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: Mom, when's dinner? I'm starving.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Twenty minutes or so, sweetie.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: We'll wrap this in time, Mag.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: How much longer till this is done?

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Another session like this. Maybe two. Then we're solid for winter.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: Then we can sleep in, right?

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: No such luck. Winter's got its own work.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: I don't like winter. It's so cold.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Winter keeps us safe, buddy. Come help me?

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: What do you need me to do?

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Wash these greens. Use the cold water from the bucket.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Finn, that bundle on the left.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: Got it! This roof's gonna be amazing.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: One beam at a time, Finn.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: That's how all buildings happen, Saw. One at a time.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Bear, dry your hands. Help me tear this fish.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: Is it the one I saw this morning?

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: I caught it! Right in the pool!

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: You sure did. Now let's cook it right.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: Can I eat it raw?

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: Gross, Bear.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: We'll cook it proper. Maggie knows best.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Just a few more minutes, everyone. Hang tight.

action: Fits the final beams of the day on the roof in the long evening light, Sawyer working steadily beside him.
thought: This roof's the spine. Nearly there.

action: Stretches foraged greens and berries into a thin, warm dinner at the porch, Bear close by and hungry.
thought: Making nothing into warmth tonight.

action: Works alongside Cole on the final roof beams, arms tired but focused, learning the finish that matters.
thought: This roof's teaching me something real.

action: Hauls materials from the build site down to the porch, arriving breathless to help Maggie with the meal prep.
thought: We're so close now. Can feel it.

action: Waits hungry and restless at the porch, helping Maggie stir and prep while stealing glances at the nearly-ready food.
thought: When do we finally get to eat?

description: As the last light stretches long, Cole and Sawyer finish the final roof beams while Maggie and Bear prepare a thin, warm dinner at the porch, Finn helping—the family converging on the meal that holds them.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: This the last one for today?

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: The last good beam. We're nearly there.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: How many more days till it's done?

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Two more days like today. Then we're weathered.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Two days? I can live with that.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: My shoulders are screaming, but I like it.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: That's the sign you're learning something real.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: Dad, why's it feel different? Like, real?

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Because you're building something that matters. Your hands are proof.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: Can we eat now? My stomach's eating itself.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Five minutes, little man. I'm stretching this as far as it goes.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: Maggie, this smells incredible. What is this?

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Foraged greens, berries, some smoked fish. Thin, but warm.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: You're magic. I've decided. You're magic.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Come on, Sawyer. Light's soft now. We're done.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: Yeah. Yeah, I need to rest.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: You worked like a man today. That's real.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: We're almost there. All of us.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Here's the day: roof's nearly done, we're all here, Maggie made warmth from almost nothing.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: We're more than standing. We're building something.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: This is the best thing ever.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: You say that every time you're hungry.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: But he's right this time.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: He's not wrong.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: Tomorrow we finish?

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Two more days. Rise early, work steady.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: We will. We have to.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: We will because we want to. That's what makes it ours.

action: Tends the fire, checking the stove's draft and the cabin's warmth as the day's work settles into evening.
thought: One more day. The roof holds us through winter.

action: Sits at the porch with Bear bundled close, keeping him warm as the light fades and the day's exhaustion settles in.
thought: They're nearly there. Just don't break yet.

action: Lingers at the porch, riding the high of the roof work, asking Cole about tomorrow's plans and what comes after.
thought: I'm learning how to build something real.

action: Leans against the cabin wall, restless with the day's buzz still alive in him, watching the light drain from the sky.
thought: One more day and the roof is ours.

action: Settles into Maggie's lap as the day fades, tired and hungry, watching the fire's glow soften into dusk.
thought: When do we get real food again?

description: The family gathers as the last light fades: Cole at the fire, Maggie and Bear at the porch with Sawyer nearby asking Cole about tomorrow, and Finn against the cabin wall; warm, exhausted, and one day from their winter shelter.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: That roof's nearly there. One more day.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Eat while it's warm. We did good today.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: One more big push and the spine is done?

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: That's it. Then we winterize the walls.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: Will we have time for a greenhouse?

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: One thing at a time, bud. Eat.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: When do we get real food again?

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: When we go to town. You did good today, buddy.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: How many days till the next run?

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Three, maybe four if the weather holds.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: Can we start the walls tomorrow?

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: The beams have to cure first. We'll prep.

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: You're all running on fumes. Rest soon.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: I'm not running. I'm sitting. And hungry.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: You're always hungry, Bear.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: Because I actually am hungry!

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Fair point. Maggie, what's for breakfast?

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Oats and the last of the honey.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: That'll hold us till the next town run?

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: It'll have to. We're making it work.

dialogue.speaker: finn
dialogue.line: I love this. Building with all of you.

dialogue.speaker: sawyer
dialogue.line: We're almost done with the hard part.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: This is the hard part. But you're holding steady.

dialogue.speaker: bear
dialogue.line: Can I go to sleep now?

dialogue.speaker: maggie
dialogue.line: Soon, honey. Drink some water first.

dialogue.speaker: cole
dialogue.line: Tomorrow's the day. Rest well, all of you.
